newsitem.title: GERMANY: German metals recyclers welcome U.S. scrap ruling.
newsitem.headline: German metals recyclers welcome U.S. scrap ruling.

text.p: German metals recyclers organised in Gesamtverband Stahl-und NE-Metall-Recycling said a United States ruling on the declassification of scrap metals from waste would help establish global clarity on the issue.
The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) earlier this month set up categories to exclude industrially produced scrap metal from waste.
Industry and trade expect easier handling and cost reductions in their operations if it can be clearly stated they are not arranging for disposal of waste.
"The U.S. ruling comes as a great relief to the international scrap-producing and trading industries," said Rolf Willeke, deputy chairman of the Gesamtverband, from his Duesseldorf office.
"It is entirely in line with our efforts to clarify legally, once and for all, that we are concerned with primary raw materials, not waste," he said on release of a press statement.
The U.S. ruling would be used as a basis for upcoming discussions with German states and the Bonn government, which aimed at laying down legal and operational rules for recycling.
The EPA ruling would also have a knock-on effect on Basle convention rules on the transport of hazardous waste as well as on OECD and European Union legislation on the status of secondary metals.
The 1,200-1,300 German steel and base metals recycling companies represented by the Gesamtverband have an estimated joint annual turnover of 15 billion marks.
